common_name: Ebony Knight Black Mondo Grass (Compact Patented Dark Selection)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery plugs in spring in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, spacing clumps a bit closer together than standard black mondo since Ebony Knight stays noticeably more compact and clump-forming.

directions: Ebony Knight is a trademarked, more compact and heavier-blooming selection of black mondo grass than the widely sold 'Nigrescens', forming tighter, denser clumps of near-black, grass-like foliage that stay shorter and tidier at the edges of a bed or path. New blades emerge green before darkening fully to black within a season, and in summer short spikes of small lilac-pink flowers rise just above the foliage, followed by the shiny black berries typical of the species. It spreads slowly by short stolons rather than running aggressively, making it well suited to small-scale edging, rock garden pockets, and container combinations where a less sprawling black mondo is wanted. Best foliage color and the tightest habit develop with consistent moisture and some shade from the hottest afternoon sun.
